rules.title: Chicago — Offer Hours to Existing Employees Before Hiring

result.summary: Before hiring new employees or using agency or temporary staff, the employer must offer additional hours to qualified existing employees

rules.title: Chicago — Schedule Change Premium (any change with <10 days notice, 2020-2022)

result.summary: 1 hour of pay at the regular rate for each shift the employer adds, moves, shortens or cancels with less than 10 days notice (notice window before 2022-07-01)

rules.title: Chicago — Schedule Change Premium (any change with <14 days notice)

result.summary: 1 hour of pay at the regular rate for each shift the employer adds, moves, shortens or cancels with less than 14 days notice (10 days from 2020-07-01 to 2022-06-30)

rules.title: Chicago — Schedule Change Premium (hours subtracted or shift cancelled with <24 hours notice)

result.summary: Half the regular rate for each scheduled hour not worked when, with less than 24 hours notice, the employer subtracts hours or cancels a shift

rules.title: Chicago — Good Faith Estimate at Hire

result.summary: Before or at hire the employer must give a written good faith estimate of the projected days and hours of work for the first 90 days, including on-call shifts

rules.title: Chicago — Right to Decline Late-Added Hours

result.summary: The employee may decline any previously unscheduled hours added with less than 14 days notice

rules.title: Los Angeles — Offer Hours to Existing Employees Before Hiring

result.summary: Before hiring new employees or contractors, the employer must offer the work in writing to current employees for 72 hours (or until accepted) when they are qualified

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Art. 5 (offer of additional work) (Fair Work Week Ordinance)

rules.title: Los Angeles — 14-Day Advance Notice Required (Retail)

result.summary: 1 hour of pay at the regular rate for each change the employer makes to a posted schedule with less than 14 days notice that adds time or changes the date, time or location with no loss of hours

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Art. 5, §185.00 et seq. (Fair Work Week Ordinance)
citations.section: LAMC Art. 5 (advance notice and predictability pay)

rules.title: Los Angeles — Schedule Change Premium (hours subtracted or shift cancelled with <14 days notice)

result.summary: Half the regular rate for each hour not worked when, with less than 14 days notice, the employer reduces a shift by at least 15 minutes or cancels it

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Art. 5 (predictability pay) (Fair Work Week Ordinance)

rules.title: Los Angeles — Good Faith Estimate at Hire

result.summary: Before hire, and within 10 days of a request, the employer must give a written good faith estimate of the employee's work schedule

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Art. 5 (good faith estimate) (Fair Work Week Ordinance)

rules.title: Los Angeles — On-Call Shift Premium (not called in)

result.summary: Half the regular rate for each scheduled hour of an on-call shift the employee is not called in to work

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Art. 5 (predictability pay) (Fair Work Week Ordinance)

rules.title: Los Angeles — Right to Decline Late-Added Hours

result.summary: The employee may decline any hours, shifts or changes not on the posted schedule or added with less than 14 days notice; the employee's consent to a change must be in writing

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Art. 5 (right to decline) (Fair Work Week Ordinance)

rules.title: NYC fast food — Offer Shifts to Existing Employees Before Hiring

result.summary: Before hiring new employees to work additional shifts, the employer must post a notice of the shifts for 3 days and offer them to current employees

rules.title: NYC Fast Food — 14-Day Advance Notice Required

result.summary: Posting fast food employee schedules with less than 14 days advance notice

rules.title: NYC fast food — Schedule Change Premium ($10: hours added or time changed, 7 to 13 days notice)

result.summary: $10 per change when, with at least 7 but less than 14 days notice, the employer adds hours or changes the date or time of a shift with no loss of hours

rules.title: NYC fast food — Schedule Change Premium ($20: hours subtracted, 7 to 13 days notice)

result.summary: $20 per change when, with at least 7 but less than 14 days notice, the employer subtracts hours or cancels a shift

rules.title: NYC fast food — Schedule Change Premium ($75: hours subtracted or shift cancelled, <24 hours notice)

result.summary: $75 per change when, with less than 24 hours notice, the employer subtracts hours or cancels a shift

rules.title: NYC fast food — Schedule Change Premium ($15: hours added or time changed, <7 days notice)

result.summary: $15 per change when, with less than 7 days notice, the employer adds hours or changes the date or time of a shift with no loss of hours

rules.title: NYC fast food — Schedule Change Premium ($45: hours subtracted, <7 days but at least 24 hours notice)

result.summary: $45 per change when, with less than 7 days but at least 24 hours notice, the employer subtracts hours or cancels a shift

rules.title: NYC fast food — Good Faith Estimate at Hire

result.summary: At hire the employer must give a written good faith estimate of the number of hours the employee can expect each week and the expected days, times and locations; an updated estimate is owed when the schedule changes significantly

rules.title: NYC fast food — Consent Required for Added Hours

result.summary: The employer may not add hours or shifts to a posted schedule without the employee's written consent; the employee may decline

rules.title: NYC Retail — 72-Hour Advance Notice Required

result.summary: Posting retail employee schedules with less than 72 hours advance notice

citations.source: NYC Admin Code §20-1251 (Fair Workweek Law, retail)

rules.title: NYC retail — No Added Shifts With <72 Hours Notice Without Written Consent

result.summary: A retail employer may not add a shift or hours with less than 72 hours notice unless the employee consents in writing

rules.title: NYC retail — No Cancelling Shifts With <72 Hours Notice

result.summary: A retail employer may not cancel, shorten or move a shift with less than 72 hours notice (except for emergencies, or when the employee asks)

rules.title: NYC Retail — On-Call Scheduling Prohibited

result.summary: Requiring retail employees to be on-call (must schedule or not schedule; cannot require availability without pay)

citations.source: NYC Admin Code §20-1252 (Fair Workweek Law, retail)

rules.title: Oregon — 14-Day Advance Notice Required

result.summary: 1 hour of pay per shift for schedule posted with less than 14 days notice

rules.title: Oregon — Schedule Change Premium (hours or shift added, or time changed, with <14 days notice)

result.summary: 1 additional hour of pay when, with less than 14 days notice, the employer adds more than 30 minutes to a shift, changes the date or start/end time with no loss of hours, or schedules an additional shift

rules.title: Oregon — Schedule Change Premium (hours subtracted or shift cancelled with <14 days notice)

result.summary: Half the regular rate for each scheduled hour not worked when, with less than 14 days notice, the employer subtracts hours, cancels a shift, or changes the date or time with a loss of hours

rules.title: Oregon — Good Faith Estimate at Hire

result.summary: At hire the employer must give a written good faith estimate of the median hours the employee can expect per month and whether the employee is on the voluntary standby list

rules.title: Oregon — On-Call Shift Premium (not called in)

result.summary: Half the regular rate for each scheduled hour of an on-call shift the employee is not asked to work (does not apply to employees on the voluntary standby list)

rules.title: Oregon — Right to Decline Unscheduled Shifts

result.summary: The employee may decline any work shift not included in the written schedule and any hours added with less than 14 days notice; the employer may not retaliate for declining

rules.title: Philadelphia — Offer Shifts to Existing Employees Before Hiring

result.summary: Before hiring new employees or using agency or temporary staff, the employer must post available shifts and offer them to existing employees for 72 hours

rules.title: Philadelphia — 14-Day Advance Notice Required

result.summary: 1 hour of pay per affected shift when the schedule is posted or changed with less than 14 days notice (10 days before 2021-01-01)

rules.title: Philadelphia — Schedule Change Premium (hours or shift added, or time changed, with <14 days notice)

result.summary: 1 hour of pay at the regular rate when, with less than 14 days notice, the employer adds time to a shift, adds a shift, or changes the date, time or location with no loss of hours (changes of 20 minutes or less are exempt)

rules.title: Philadelphia — Schedule Change Premium (hours subtracted or shift cancelled with <14 days notice)

result.summary: Half the regular rate for each hour not worked when, with less than 14 days notice, the employer subtracts hours or cancels a shift

rules.title: Philadelphia — Good Faith Estimate at Hire

result.summary: At hire the employer must give a written good faith estimate of the average weekly hours over a typical 90-day period, whether on-call shifts are expected, and the expected days and times

rules.title: Philadelphia — On-Call Shift Premium (not called in)

result.summary: Half the regular rate for each scheduled hour of an on-call shift the employee is not called in to work

rules.title: Philadelphia — Right to Decline Late-Added Hours

result.summary: The employee may decline any hours or shifts not on the posted schedule or added with less than 14 days notice; added hours require written consent

rules.title: Seattle — Offer Hours to Existing Employees Before Hiring

result.summary: Before hiring new employees or using staffing agencies, the employer must post a notice of available hours for 3 days and offer them to qualified existing employees

rules.title: Seattle — 14-Day Advance Notice Required

result.summary: 1 hour of pay per shift for schedule posted with less than 14 days notice

rules.title: Seattle — Schedule Change Premium (hours or shift added, or time changed, with <14 days notice)

result.summary: 1 additional hour of pay when, with less than 14 days notice, the employer adds hours, adds a shift, or changes the date, time or location of a shift without reducing hours

rules.title: Seattle — Schedule Change Premium (hours subtracted with <14 days notice)

result.summary: 50% of pay for subtracted/cancelled hours (predictability pay)

rules.title: Seattle — Good Faith Estimate at Hire

result.summary: At hire the employer must give a written good faith estimate of the employee's expected median hours and whether on-call shifts are expected; it must be revisited yearly and when a significant change occurs

rules.title: Seattle — On-Call Shift Premium (not called in)

result.summary: Half the regular rate for each scheduled hour of an on-call shift the employee is not called in to work

rules.title: Seattle — Right to Decline Late-Added Hours

result.summary: The employee may decline any hours or shifts not on the posted schedule or added with less than 14 days notice

rules.title: San Francisco — Offer Hours to Part-Time Employees Before Hiring

result.summary: Before hiring new employees or using staffing agencies, the employer must offer additional hours in writing to qualified current part-time employees (fewer than 35 hours a week)

citations.source: San Francisco Formula Retail Employee Rights Ordinances (Police Code Art. 33F-33G, recodified in the Labor and Employment Code)

rules.title: San Francisco — 14-Day Advance Notice of Work Schedule

result.summary: Work schedules must be posted at least 14 days (2 weeks) before the first shift on them

citations.source: San Francisco Formula Retail Employee Rights Ordinances (Police Code Art. 33F-33G, recodified in the Labor and Employment Code)

rules.title: San Francisco — Schedule Change Premium (4 hours: <24 hours notice, shift over 4 hours)

result.summary: 4 hours of pay at the regular rate when a shift longer than 4 hours is changed with less than 24 hours notice

citations.source: San Francisco Formula Retail Employee Rights Ordinances (Police Code Art. 33F-33G, recodified in the Labor and Employment Code)

rules.title: San Francisco — Schedule Change Premium (2 hours: <24 hours notice, shift of 4 hours or less)

result.summary: 2 hours of pay at the regular rate when a shift of 4 hours or less is changed with less than 24 hours notice

citations.source: San Francisco Formula Retail Employee Rights Ordinances (Police Code Art. 33F-33G, recodified in the Labor and Employment Code)

rules.title: San Francisco — Schedule Change Premium (1 hour: <7 days but at least 24 hours notice)

result.summary: 1 hour of pay at the regular rate for each shift changed with less than 7 days but at least 24 hours notice (added, moved, cut or cancelled)

citations.source: San Francisco Formula Retail Employee Rights Ordinances (Police Code Art. 33F-33G, recodified in the Labor and Employment Code)

rules.title: San Francisco — Good Faith Estimate at Hire

result.summary: Before hire the employer must give a written good faith estimate of the expected minimum number of scheduled shifts per month and their days and hours

citations.source: San Francisco Formula Retail Employee Rights Ordinances (Police Code Art. 33F-33G, recodified in the Labor and Employment Code)

rules.title: San Francisco — On-Call Shift Premium (4 hours: not called in, shift over 4 hours)

result.summary: 4 hours of pay at the regular rate for an on-call shift longer than 4 hours the employee is not called in to work

citations.source: San Francisco Formula Retail Employee Rights Ordinances (Police Code Art. 33F-33G, recodified in the Labor and Employment Code)

rules.title: San Francisco — On-Call Shift Premium (2 hours: not called in, shift of 4 hours or less)

result.summary: 2 hours of pay at the regular rate for an on-call shift of 4 hours or less the employee is not called in to work

citations.source: San Francisco Formula Retail Employee Rights Ordinances (Police Code Art. 33F-33G, recodified in the Labor and Employment Code)
